Reference - Authors: Ingeborg Zehbe; Andreas M Kaufmann; Markus Schmidt; Hanni Hohn; Markus J Maeurer
Reference - Title: Human papillomavirus 16 E6-specific CD45RA+ CCR7+ high avidity CD8+ T cells fail to control tumor growth despite interferon-gamma production in patients with cervical cancer.
Immunization - Comments: Peripheral blood and lymph node samples were collected from 5 HLA-A*0201-matched women with invasive HPV16 positive cervical cancer were obtained from the Department of Gynecology at the University of Mainz.
Assay - Comments: CD8+ T cells from all 5 patients recognized C1RA2 cells pulsed with the epitope irrespective of the APC type or T-cell compartment (PBL, TIL or T-LN) albeit at different levels. The data suggest that the epitope is naturally processed and present. Moreover, epitope-specific T cells were of high avidity, though reactivity and target cell recognition can vary with regard to anatomic compartments within the same patient. Epitope-specific T cells were found to reside preferentially within the CD45RA+ CCR7+ T-cell sub-population of all tissue types examined.

Reference - Title: Landscape of immunogenic tumor antigens in successful immunotherapy of virally induced epithelial cancer.
Immunization - Comments: Two patients were studied with HPV+ metastatic cervical carcinoma who experienced complete cancer regression that is ongoing, 44 (patient 3775 with HPV16+ squamous cell carcinoma) and 37 (patient 3853 with HPV18+ adenocarcinoma) months after adoptive transfer of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL). The infused cells, TIL-3775 and TIL-3853, consisted of T cells expanded from TIL cultures selected for reactivity against the HPV-E6 and/or -E7 oncoproteins. However, these cultures also contained T cells with initially uncharacterized antigen specificities. TIL-3775 were enriched by selecting for T cells expressing CD137 upon co-culture of TIL-3775 with DCs electroporated with full-length versions of HPV-encoded genes and expanded in vitro for 14 days. The TCRA and TCRB chain pairs were sequenced from single-cell sorted activated T cells and transduced into primary T cells.
Assay - Comments: The minimal 9-mer peptide epitope was predicted to bind with the highest affinity to one of patient’s HLA-class I alleles was synthesized. The epitope activated CD8+ T cells transduced with the TCR, analyzed by CD137 expression.
